agent.problem: Most of the choices are not informed guesses. Cards 2, 8, 13, 15 and 17 depend on discovering details that the earlier cards have not supplied, while cards 4 and 7 ask for unseen wording. Only cards 10, 12, 16 and 19 clearly give the baker enough context to reason toward an answer. Add context or replace some questions so that discovery questions remain the exception.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The baker has not yet been told what the Levites receive, and the earlier cards provide no way to reason out both cities and pasturelands. Tents and wells also make plausible sense in the blanks, so this tests wording the baker has not seen rather than meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker distinguish an honest report from an alarming or unfinished one. The blank simply asks for the unseen adjective in verse 7.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Calling the fearful group "the other spies" implies every spy except Caleb, which would sweep Joshua into that group. Verse 8 more precisely identifies them as the brothers who went with Caleb; the retelling should not broaden the group beyond what the text says.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

agent.problem: The card cites only verse 15, but its second sentence also retells the forty-five-year wait from verse 10 and the completed inheritance from verses 13-14. Replace that recap with a reaction grounded in the rest from war, or otherwise make the card's content and citation agree.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
